validated_work_order.understanding:
#71's PR (#73) merged with seven review findings and one QA finding open; this ticket is the lot. I re-verified every claim against the current tree before writing this, and prototyped the replacement parser end to end rather than taking either document's word for it.

The ticket is two independent defects wearing one ticket's clothing. Six of the eight findings are the same defect: test/web/pages.test.js reads src/web/styles.css in EIGHT places and hand-rolls a parser at each one, and four of the parsers are weaker than their neighbour in a different direction. Finding 1 (a px/rem floor passes a test whose message says 'twelve characters'), finding 3 (an at-rule override is invisible to the card pin's later-override check), finding 4 and finding 5 (the min-width pin does not strip comments, so a comment can be the ONLY mention of a floor and the rule still reads green), and finding 6 (four near-identical parsers) are one root cause: ad-hoc regexes where one shared, comment-stripping, brace-depth-aware reader belongs.

The remaining two are one CSS declaration. Review finding 2 and the QA finding are the same defect reported twice: .awaiting-list is display: grid, its li are grid items, and the free text it prints is the decision_id in a <strong> — the same shape as the four lists the wrap rule names, in a fifth list it does not name.

Two things neither document had quite right. First, the plan routed the shared reader through FIVE of the eight read sites; I confirmed the count and reproduced the false green in two of the three it skipped (#main:focus and .page-title both go green with their pinned declaration deleted outright and a comment left in its place). Closing the class in five places and leaving it open in three is not closing it. Second, the plan's acceptance criteria stated pass counts and a green baseline that do not hold: the file is 72 tests / 71 pass / 1 fail today, and the plan both calls that 72/72 and asserts the totals stay at 471 across the suite while adding a test that makes them 472.

One defect the ticket does not mention at all: 'the approval action row can shrink, and the selectors below have something to match' is RED on main, and has been since the commit that introduced it (e29106f). It is the test that holds the min-width pin, so the pin this ticket exists to repair has not been running green. It is one line, and it is in scope, because nothing else here is verifiable while it is red.
validated_work_order.root_cause:
Two independent causes.

(1) PRODUCT DEFECT, one declaration. src/web/styles.css scopes overflow-wrap: anywhere to four card classes (.experiment-card, .opportunity-row, .approval-card, .learning-card) at the .experiment-card, .opportunity-row, .approval-card, .learning-card rule. .awaiting-list is display: grid (styles.css:455) and .awaiting-list li (styles.css:463) carries no overflow-wrap, so a grid item is floored at its min-content width and one long unbreakable decision_id — the same free text the four named lists already wrap — sizes the whole track. The QA report and the review measure it independently at different fixture lengths (1443px at 120 characters, 1672px at 140) and agree on the mechanism; I confirmed the shape from the CSS. A grid item's automatic minimum is the token's min-content width, which is precisely what overflow-wrap: anywhere removes and break-word does not.

(2) TEST-INFRASTRUCTURE DEFECT, one missing abstraction, in EIGHT places not five. test/web/pages.test.js reads src/web/styles.css at lines 345, 359, 1633, 1653, 1693, 1757, 1802 and 1819 and builds its own regex for selectors, bodies or declarations each time. The card pin at 1693 had to grow three defensive layers — comment stripping, exact-compound selector matching, a scoped later-override check — precisely because its parse was the weakest; the other seven re-derive weaker versions of those same three things from raw text. Findings 1, 3, 4 and 5 are each a specific way one of those weaker parses returns a false green, and I reproduced all four plus two more of the same shape that the ticket never named.
validated_work_order.approach:
Three changes, one per root cause. Everything below that says 'the shared reader' means the same two helpers, and every pin in the file uses them — there is no second parser left at the end of this change.

A. Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere;` to `.awaiting-list li` in src/web/styles.css, with a comment in the same voice and for the same reason as the existing wrap rule: a grid item is floored at its min-content width, the decision_id is free text, `anywhere` rather than `break-word` because break-word leaves intrinsic sizing alone. One declaration. Then pin it in the house style, and give the pin the render half so it is a fact about the page and not about the file: render /journal with override 'partial' against the seeded repositories and require class="awaiting-list" and an <li data-decision-id=...> whose <strong> holds the decision_id. The critic confirmed by execution that this reaches the surface from the existing seed (dec_seed_awaiting_1 renders inside data-testid="journal-awaiting"), so no new fixture is needed. Do NOT fold .awaiting-list li into the four-class card rule: that rule's assertion requires exactly those four bare selectors, and a descendant selector on a different structural shape would satisfy a selector the pages never render as a bare class.

B. Add three shared helpers near the top of test/web/pages.test.js, beside the existing H1_HOOK and mainOf helpers, each with a comment naming the two things it defends against — comments, and nesting — and route ALL EIGHT styles.css tests through them: the #main:focus suppression (345), the forced-colors carve-out (359), .page-title (1633), #main > * and .table-scroll (1653), the card wrap (1693), .approval-actions and .approval-actions input (1757), .journal-drawer-body (1802) and .tenant-name (1819). Keep every existing assertion and every existing failure message verbatim; only the plumbing moves.

  `cssRules(css)` strips /* */ comments first, then walks the source with a brace stack. A rule inside an at-rule is emitted with its OWN selector and a `nested: true` flag, so `@media (max-width: 900px) { .approval-card { overflow-wrap: normal } }` is a rule whose selector is `.approval-card`, not one whose selector is the at-rule prelude. The current /([^{}]+)\{([^}]*)\}/g pattern captures that media block as a single rule with selector `@media (max-width: 900px)` and a body of literal text, which is exactly why the card pin's override filter finds no card class and passes. Every rule carries a source `index` so the later-override ordering is preserved.

  I prototyped this and ran it against the current stylesheet, because the proposal asserted the replacement's behaviour rather than showing it. It emits 66 rules in source order; every one of the nine pinned selectors resolves; the six nested rules (.the forced-colors #main:focus, .skeleton, #journal-drawer, .journal-filters .journal-filter-control, .kpi-strip, #main) are emitted with their own selectors. The @media override mutation is caught; a benign `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` passes both at top level and nested inside an at-rule, which matters because the card pin was deliberately widened to stop failing on unrelated rules. Two implementation notes from that prototype, both mine and neither in either document: (1) the state machine must treat ';' as the terminator of a declaration and '{' as the terminator of a selector — a naive 'append everything to the parent body' version silently drops every nested rule and reintroduces finding 3 exactly; (2) @keyframes skeleton-pulse contributes `0%` and `100%` step selectors to the rule list. Those are harmless because every lookup is an exact selector match against a pinned selector, but say so in a comment so the next reader does not go looking for the bug.

  `declarations(body, prop)` matches a single property's values inside an already comment-stripped rule body. This is the fix for findings 4 and 5: the min-width pin currently runs /min-width\s*:\s*([^;]+);/ over the RAW body, so a rule with no min-width at all but a comment naming one reads as ['16ch'], count 1, green — the BUG-1 state passing the BUG-1 pin — and a comment beside a real declaration is counted as the declaration. I reproduced both against the exact current parse.

  `laterOverrides(rules, rule, selectors)` is the third helper, and it is the critique's most useful structural change: the card pin's override loop is currently per-test local code scoped to CARD_CLASSES, so migrating the parsers without lifting that loop would reintroduce the same blind spot on every pin the change touches, and on the NEW .awaiting-list li pin this ticket adds. One shared function, called by each pin with its own selector set, is the only version that stops the drift rather than relocating it. I checked the cost of adding it to the migrated pins: in the current stylesheet, zero later same-selector rules exist for .page-title, #main > *, .table-scroll, .approval-actions, .approval-actions input, .journal-drawer-body and .tenant-name, so every one of those checks passes green today. The single exception is #main:focus, whose later same-selector rule is the intentional @media (forced-colors: active) carve-out — and that pairing is already the subject of its own test's source-order assertion, so the override check must not be added blindly to it (see below).

  THE FORCED-COLORS PIN IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS CARE, NOT A MECHANICAL SWAP. Its current `[^@]*?` regex plus a `carveOut.index > bareRuleAt` comparison is the only place in the file that deliberately reasons about at-rule nesting, and it is the only thing in the suite pinning that the carve-out comes AFTER the bare rule at equal specificity. Rewrite it against the shared reader's nested/index data — the bare #main:focus and the nested one are both emitted, in source order, with distinct indices, so `nestedIndex > bareIndex` expresses the same assertion using data the helper already produces — and the assertion itself must survive. Removing it would leave the landmark as the one focusable element with no indicator under forced-colors, with a green suite.

  CRITICAL: the helper's selector lookup must anchor on the SELECTOR'S END, not `includes()`. '.opportunity-roww' and '.tenant-names' both contain their pinned selector as a substring, and an `includes()` lookup would silently delete the rename protection the current `\s*\{` anchors give every pin in the file — one bug, all eight pins, and it would be invisible because nothing else in the suite catches a rename.

C. Fix the pre-existing red test, because nothing else in this change is verifiable while it is red — AC-3 and AC-5 both read the file's totals, and a red file makes every count in this work order ambiguous. The assertion is /<li class="approval-card">/ and the markup is `<li class="approval-card" data-testid="approval-card" data-approval-card data-approval-id=... data-tenant-id=...>`: a qa/selectors.md-stable data-testid was added to the element after the matcher was written, and the matcher anchors on the closing '>'. The fix is /<li class="approval-card"[\s>]/, matching the class attribute followed by a boundary rather than the end of the tag. (\b does not work and the reason is worth keeping in a comment: after the closing quote both the quote and the following space are non-word characters, so there is no word boundary there.) While in that helper, drop the `approval.requested` raw-event append from pendingApprovalRepos — grep for that event type across src/ returns nothing, and replayRawToDerived derives only spend, so it is dead weight that reads as load-bearing — and rewrite the docstring at the top of the helper that explains the append, which is itself stale: it points at 'the read at src/web/pages.js:924' and line 924 is experiment-card markup. The seed is what supplies the card: SEEDED_PENDING_IDS holds THREE pending approvals (apv_seed_budget_1, apv_seed_campaign_1, apv_seed_geography_1) and SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS holds four including SEEDED_LAPSED_ID. Do not write 'four pending' anywhere — it is three pending, four seeded, one lapsed. The critic confirmed by execution that removing the append still renders 3 approval-cards, 3 approval-actions forms, 3 reason inputs and 2 buttons per row, so both callers stay satisfied.

risks: Narrowing the min-width regex to ch-only is a behaviour change to a test, not a pure strengthening, and it is the decision here I most want a human to look at. A defensible `min-width: 96px` will now fail the pin and has to be written as `12ch`. I upheld it over the reviewer's first option (convert px and rem with a hard-coded ratio) because the input is `font: inherit` and the root font-size is a browser default, so nothing in the file fixes the conversion: 1ch measured 10.18px for system-ui at 16px on this runner against the reviewer's suggested 8.9. A test carrying a runner-specific ratio would be green here and wrong elsewhere, and green in the direction that matters — a genuinely too-narrow floor whose px value happens to clear the ratio. Accepting px is precisely how `min-width: 12px`, the original defect, stays green. This is a judgement about a test's strictness, not a verified defect, and it is cheap to overrule.

The shared reader is a real parser where the file had regexes, and the regression I hit while prototyping is the one to expect: a naive implementation that appends nested text to the parent body silently drops every nested rule and reintroduces review finding 3 exactly, while still passing every test in the file as written today. That is why the two at-rule mutation cases are in tests[] and AC-3 is written to be read by test name.

The helper's selector lookup must anchor on the selector's end. Written as `includes()`, it silently deletes the rename protection the current `\s*\{` anchors give all eight pins at once, and nothing else in the suite catches a rename. This is the highest-leverage single line in the change.

Migrating all eight pins, not five, is the scope the critique argued for and I upheld it. It is a larger diff than the proposal asked for, and it touches the forced-colors test, the one place in the file with deliberate at-rule reasoning. The reviewer should read the assertions, not the plumbing: every assertion and failure message is meant to be preserved verbatim.

The pin for .awaiting-list li asserts 'anywhere and nothing else', which is the same brittleness the #48 and #71 pins accepted deliberately — adding a second declaration to that rule for an unrelated reason turns the suite red. House style, followed here, but a cost rather than a free win.
out_of_scope: Review finding 6's calibration panel: measured, not a defect, so nothing is added. There is no .journal-calibration class in src/web/styles.css or src/web/pages.js — the only match in the tree is the unrelated data-testid 'journal-calibration-refreshing' at pages.js:662. The panel is a plain .panel (display: block) whose three strings come from calibrationReport() (src/domain/decisions.js:377) formatted with toFixed(2) and integer counts, so no input can make them long; the longest whitespace-delimited token measured 18 characters and no element exceeded its own client box. Adding overflow-wrap to it would be a declaration against a defect that does not exist. Recorded so the next run inherits the answer instead of the gap — and AC-10 plus qa_script step 11 measure it anyway rather than taking this paragraph's word for it.

`min-width: calc(...)` stays rejected by the narrowed pin. A calc() expression is not measurable by a test that has no font, and the pin's job is to fail loudly on a floor it cannot verify rather than to pass on one it cannot check. Recorded as an accepted cost next to the px narrowing, not as an oversight.

The browser measurement of the fix is not in CI and this ticket does not put it there. AC-1, AC-2 and AC-10 are browser-verified by the qa_script; the rest are test-verified. Closing the browser/CI gap for the whole family of narrow-viewport pins is a separate ticket, and no single follow-up should quietly claim to close it for surfaces it did not measure.

`.awaiting-list` renders only under ?state=partial, which is reachable through the QA preview override and by the in-app link at pages.js:708 from an empty journal, but never from the default /journal. The defect and the fix are both real and both reachable; whether the default journal should also surface awaiting-maturity decisions is a product question about the partial shell, not a wrapping bug.

The four card classes stay four. .awaiting-list li is a descendant selector on a different structural shape (a list item inside a grid list, not a card), and folding it into the card wrap rule would make that pin's exact-compound-match assertion — the one #71 added to survive a rename — match a selector the pages never render as a bare class.
No change to the min-width declaration itself. 16ch stays 16ch; this change fixes the test that reads it and adds the one missing CSS declaration, and does not re-tune the floor.

No change to scripts/seed.js. SEEDED_PENDING_IDS holds three pending approvals and SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS four including the lapsed one; the dead `approval.requested` append lives in the test helper, not the seed, and the seed already supplies every card the assertions need.

alternatives_considered.approach: Convert px and rem to a character count inside the min-width assertion (the reviewer's first option: ch as-is, rem as 16ch, px as px/8.9, against a 12ch threshold).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The conversion ratio is a property of the font, not of the stylesheet. The input is `font: inherit` and the root font-size is a browser default, so nothing in the file fixes the number — 1ch measured 10.18px for system-ui at 16px on this runner, against the reviewer's suggested 8.9, which is the size of the disagreement. A test carrying a hard-coded ratio would be green here and wrong on another platform's system-ui, and green in exactly the direction that matters: a genuinely too-narrow floor whose px value happens to clear the ratio. Accepting ch only makes the assertion say what it means.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep eight separate parsers and fix each finding in place: strip comments in the min-width pin and in #main:focus and .page-title, add a brace-depth scan to the card pin alone, leave the rest as they are.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That is findings 1, 3, 4 and 5 patched individually and finding 6 left open. I confirmed the skip is not harmless: #main:focus and .page-title both go green with their pinned declaration deleted and a comment in its place, and both miss a later top-level override. Eight parsers, each weaker in its own direction, guaranteed to drift again on the next stylesheet edit.

alternatives_considered.approach: Migrate the five pins the proposal named and leave #main:focus, the forced-colors carve-out and .page-title as they are, to keep the diff small.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Rejected as a scope decision, not a cost one. The ticket exists to close a class of false green, and leaving three parsers behind reopens that class in three places — two of which I reproduced going green with the declaration deleted. I checked that the marginal cost is small: all nine pinned selectors resolve under the shared reader, and in the current stylesheet no later same-selector rule exists for .page-title, #main > *, .table-scroll, .approval-actions, .approval-actions input, .journal-drawer-body or .tenant-name, so every added override check passes green today. The only exception is #main:focus, whose one later same-selector rule is the intentional forced-colors carve-out already covered by its own ordering test.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 3, take the reviewer's cheaper alternative: assert outright that the stylesheet contains no at-rule block naming a card class, with a message saying the parser cannot see inside one.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It closes the false green by forbidding a legitimate edit. A media query that adjusts a card's padding or grid placement is reasonable and would turn the suite red, and the card pin had already been deliberately widened to stop failing on unrelated rules — this would undo that in the other direction. The brace-stack walk catches the actual override and leaves benign at-rule content alone; I verified both directions against the current stylesheet.

alternatives_considered.approach: For finding 4 and 5, strip comments with the one-line `css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, ' ')` already sitting in the card pin, without a shared reader.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It fixes the two named findings and leaves the six other parsers — including the two the ticket does not name, which have the identical blind spot. It is finding 6 left open with extra steps.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the product defect in JavaScript — truncate or break the decision_id server-side before it reaches the page.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would hide stored data at the render boundary, and the same decision_id is already printed in full on the other four lists, where the fix is a stylesheet declaration. Truncation also loses information a user may need to quote into a reason. The defect is a layout one and belongs in the layout.

alternatives_considered.approach: Widen the wrap rule to a blanket `.panel *` or add overflow-wrap to #main, covering every free-text surface at once instead of naming surfaces one at a time.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The existing comment in the stylesheet records why this was rejected before: a blanket wrap reaches the table cells and makes every wide table wrap inside the page instead of scrolling in its own .table-scroll region. Naming the surface is the house pattern here, and the review's own central complaint — a surface nobody measured reads as a surface with no defect — is answered by measuring and naming.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the pre-existing red test alone and file it separately, on the grounds that it is not in the ticket's list of findings.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is the test that holds the min-width pin this ticket exists to repair. Its being red is why nobody noticed the pin's false greens, and shipping a fix to a pin that is not running green makes the fix unverifiable — a QA reading 'the file is red' could not tell whether AC-3's mutation was caught or the baseline was already failing. It is one line.

alternatives_considered.approach: Give each migrated pin its own inline later-override loop, as the card pin has today, rather than a shared laterOverrides() helper.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That is finding 6's exact shape reproduced inside the fix for finding 6: eight copies of a small thing, and the copy the plan is adding right now would be the ninth. It also fails the critique's structural point — the new .awaiting-list pin would get its own copy, and the next ticket's pin would get a ninth.

alternatives_considered.approach: Have the new .awaiting-list render half create its own awaiting decision through the repository instead of relying on the seed's dec_seed_awaiting_1, so a future seed cleanup cannot turn the pin red for an unrelated reason.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A real fragility, but a small one, and the same fragility every existing render half in this file carries — the card pin already depends on the seed rendering four card classes. Both paths are constructible (the critic verified a 140-character decision_id is accepted by repositories.decisions.create with no validation error), so the choice is convention. I kept seededRepos and recorded the dependency in residual_risks rather than adding a fixture only this test uses.

assumptions: The `ch` unit is the correct unit for the pin's stated property, resting on `ch` being the advance width of '0' in the element's font. I did not verify that this holds for every glyph in the reason field — a reason is typed text, not zeroes, and the two differ in width. The 59px-versus-162.9px contrast that motivates the pin is measured; the 'twelve characters' phrasing is the pin's own and I kept it rather than restating it in a unit I cannot measure per-glyph.

Narrowing the min-width regex to ch-only does not block a legitimate future edit. I judged a px floor a restatement in ch rather than a loss, but that is a judgement about this repo's habit, not something the code or the docs settle.

Migrating all eight pins, not five, is the right scope for this ticket. The ticket's own subject is the class of false green, and a shared reader applied to five of eight sites leaves the class open in three places — two of which I reproduced going green with their declaration deleted.

The pre-existing red test is a stale matcher and not a deliberate pin. The evidence is that the element carries a qa/selectors.md-stable data-testid the matcher cannot see, and that the file goes 72/72 when the matcher is corrected. I did not find a commit that deliberately narrowed it, and I did not exhaustively search the sdlc-state branch's history for one.

The new .awaiting-list li pin asserting 'anywhere and nothing else' is the right strictness. I am following the pattern of the #48 and #71 pins, which the reviewer did not object to; if the house style is loosening, this pin is stricter than it needs to be.
unknowns: Whether a decision_id in a real deployment can actually reach 120+ unbreakable characters. The repository accepts any string and the API auto-creates tenants from free-text request headers, so a long id is constructible; whether it occurs in practice is a production question I have no access to. The defect is real and reachable either way, and its severity is unchanged by how often it fires — the same argument the QA report made when it rated the finding minor.

Whether 1ch = 10.18px holds on the platforms this app actually runs on. It is a property of the resolved system-ui font and will differ on macOS and Windows. This is precisely why the pin does not hard-code a ratio — but it does mean the twelve-character threshold is font-relative by construction, and someone revisiting the floor should measure rather than assume.

Whether the browser figures (1672, 1629, 305/360/399) match a headed browser rather than headless Chromium on this runner. I did not re-measure them — no browser driver is in the repo and dependencies are express only — but the defect is confirmed from two independent sources: the reviewer's 1672 at 140 characters and QA's 1443 at 120, plus my own reading of the CSS shape (.awaiting-list is display: grid, .awaiting-list li carries no overflow-wrap). Font rasterization and scrollbar handling can differ; the layout mechanism, a grid item floored at min-content, is not browser-specific.

Whether anything outside this repository reads the `approval.requested` raw event the test helper appends. Within src/ nothing does, and the critic rendered /approvals without it and got the three cards both callers assert on. If an external consumer exists, removing the append from a test fixture is still correct — a fixture should not be the only producer of a contract — but I cannot see outside the tree.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Every claim in this work order I re-checked myself against the current tree rather than taking either document's word: all eight styles.css read sites and the line numbers, the six reproduced false greens (the min-width unit false green, the min-width comment false green, the at-rule blind spot, and the two the ticket never named), the pre-existing red test and its 470/471 baseline, the seed's three-pending/four-seeded split, and the '\b does not work' reason. Most usefully, I prototyped the shared reader the plan only asserted and ran it against the real stylesheet: 66 rules in source order, all nine pinned selectors resolving, nested at-rule rules emitted with their own selectors, zero spurious later overrides on the seven pins that get a new check, the forced-colors ordering expressible from the new index data, the at-rule mutation caught and both benign mutations still green. That is what holds this at 88 rather than lower — the largest implementation risk in the plan is now demonstrated rather than claimed. It is not 90 because two things are unverified by me: I did not re-measure the browser figures, and the ch-only narrowing is a judgement about a test's strictness rather than a verified defect. A human who disagrees with ch-only can overrule it without touching anything else. Moving up would need a headed-browser confirmation of the three widths; moving down would need a reason to think the seed's awaiting decision or the exact-selector anchoring is less stable than I measured.
evidence: the eight read sites: grep for styles.css in test/web/pages.test.js returns 8 hits at lines 345, 359, 1633, 1653, 1693, 1757, 1802, 1819. The plan routed five and named none of 345, 359, 1633. This is the fact the whole scope change turns on.

min-width unit false green (review finding 1): ran the current parse at test/web/pages.test.js:1766-1773 over the shipped stylesheet. Mutating `min-width: 16ch` -> `min-width: 12px` yields widths ['12px'], the regex matches, and Number(floor[1]) >= 12 is TRUE. The pin is green on the defect it was written to replace.

at-rule blind spot (review finding 3): appended `@media (max-width: 900px) { .approval-card { overflow-wrap: normal; } }` and ran the card pin's own parse. It captures the media block as ONE rule whose selector is '@media (max-width: 900px)' with a body of literal text; the complete captured selector list is [.tenant-name, the four-card group, .journal-drawer-body, @media (max-width: 900px)]; the later-override filter returns [[],[]] and the assertion passes. Under the replacement reader the same injection is caught, while `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` passes both at top level and inside an at-rule.

min-width comment blindness, false-green direction (review finding 4): removed `min-width: 16ch;` from `.approval-actions input` and left `/* floor was min-width: 16ch; do not lower */`. The current regex returns ['16ch'], count 1 — both the exactly-one and the floor assertion pass. That is the BUG-1 state, no floor at all, passing the BUG-1 pin.

min-width comment blindness, consistency direction (review finding 5): inserted `/* raised to 20ch; see ticket */` above the real declaration. The current regex returns ['16ch'] — the comment consumed as the declaration, the real one not separately counted.

#main:focus comment blindness, NOT named in the ticket: deleted `outline: none;` and left `/* outline: none; was the old value */`. /#main:focus\s*\{([^}]*)\}/ still matches at line 346 and /outline:\s*none\s*;/ is TRUE against the comment. The declaration is gone and the pin is GREEN.

.page-title comment blindness, NOT named in the ticket: deleted `margin: 0;` and left `/* margin: 0; */`. /\.page-title\s*\{([^}]*)\}/ still matches at line 1634 and /margin:\s*0\s*;/ is TRUE. GREEN with the declaration gone.

first-match-only parsing, NOT named in the ticket: appended `.page-title { margin: 4rem; }`. The pin reads the ORIGINAL rule and reports `margin: 0` as present — the page breaks and the suite is green. Same for `#main:focus { outline: 3px solid red; }`.

pre-existing red test, not in the ticket: on clean main (632153e, working tree clean apart from untracked plan/) `node --test` reads 471 tests / 470 pass / 1 fail and `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` reads 72 / 71 / 1. The failure is 'the approval action row can shrink, and the selectors below have something to match' at the assertion /<li class="approval-card">/; the markup is `<li class="approval-card" data-testid="approval-card" data-approval-card data-approval-id=... data-tenant-id=...>`. The proposal checked out e29106f, the commit that introduced the assertion, and it fails there too, so it has never been green. /<li class="approval-card"[\s>]/ matches the shipped markup; /<li class="approval-card">/ does not; /<li class="approval-card"\b/ does not, because after the closing quote both the quote and the following space are non-word characters and there is no boundary.

seed split, correcting the proposal: scripts/seed.js SEEDED_PENDING_IDS holds 3 entries (apv_seed_budget_1, apv_seed_campaign_1, apv_seed_geography_1) and SEEDED_APPROVAL_IDS holds 4 including SEEDED_LAPSED_ID. Three pending, four seeded, one lapsed. The conclusion the proposal drew from 'four' — that the card renders without the dead raw-event append — is unaffected and the critic confirmed it by rendering /approvals without the append (3 cards, 3 forms, 3 reason inputs, 2 buttons per row).

the replacement reader, prototyped and run against the real stylesheet (mine, not in either document): it emits 66 rules in source order; the six rules nested inside at-rules (.skeleton, #main:focus, #journal-drawer, .journal-filters .journal-filter-control, .kpi-strip, #main) are emitted with their own selectors and a nested flag. The bare #main:focus lands at index 14 with body `outline: none;` and the forced-colors carve-out at index 15, nested, with body `outline: 2px solid CanvasText;` — so the source-order assertion survives the rewrite as a comparison of two indices the helper already produces, without the old `[^@]*?` regex. All nine pinned selectors resolve exactly once except .experiment-card, which correctly matches two rules, and #main:focus, which correctly matches two.

the cost of adding a later-override check to the migrated pins (mine): in the current stylesheet there are ZERO later same-selector rules for .page-title, #main > *, .table-scroll, .approval-actions, .approval-actions input, .journal-drawer-body and .tenant-name, so every one of those checks passes green today and only fails on a real override. The single exception is #main:focus, whose later same-selector rule is the intentional forced-colors carve-out.
comment-stripping is a no-op for the two oldest pins: the #main > * and .table-scroll bodies are byte-identical before and after stripping, so migrating them carries no comment-related regression.

the .awaiting-list defect, from the CSS rather than from a browser: .awaiting-list is display: grid (styles.css:455) and .awaiting-list li (styles.css:463) declares no overflow-wrap, which is the shape the wrap rule exists to defeat. The markup is pages.js:695-697, a <ul class="awaiting-list"> whose <strong> holds the decision_id. Two independent measurements agree on the mechanism at different fixture lengths — the review's 1672px at 140 characters and QA's 1443px at 120 — with a short-id control reading 305/320 and zero offenders in both.

calibration panel, answering the reviewer's open question (review finding 6 addendum): grep for journal-calibration finds only the unrelated data-testid 'journal-calibration-refreshing' at pages.js:662; there is no such class in the stylesheet. The panel is a plain .panel, display block, and its three strings come from calibrationReport() (src/domain/decisions.js:377) formatted with toFixed(2) and integer counts, so no input can make them long; the longest whitespace-delimited token measured 18 characters with no element exceeding its client box. No declaration added — and AC-10 and qa_script step 11 measure it regardless.
residual_risks: Every browser figure in this order (1672, 1629, 305/360/399, the six-route sweep, 1ch = 10.18px) comes from headless Chromium driven over raw CDP, because the repo has no browser driver and dependencies are express only. I did not re-measure any of them. Font rasterization and scrollbar metrics can differ from a headed browser, though the layout mechanism — a grid item floored at its min-content width — is not browser-specific. QA should confirm against a real browser rather than take these numbers as the acceptance.

The awaiting-maturity panel renders only under ?state=partial, which resolveState (pages.js:22-29) returns only from the ?state= query override; with no override it returns 'ideal' or 'empty'. AC-1, AC-2 and AC-10 are browser-verifiable only through that override. A reviewer who opens the default /journal and sees no panel has not found the fix missing. The qa_script says so at step 3.

The new pin's render half depends on the seed still containing an awaiting-maturity decision (dec_seed_awaiting_1). That is the same seed dependency the existing card pin carries, so it is house convention rather than a new hazard, but a future seed cleanup would turn this pin red for a reason unrelated to the CSS.

The shared reader is a convention, not an enforcement. Nothing stops a later ticket adding a ninth stylesheet pin with a fresh regex, which is finding 6 recurring one ticket later. The helper docstring should say so; this change cannot make it structural.

The 1672px figure is fixture-specific. 140 'q' characters is one unbreakable token; a decision_id of combining marks or zero-width characters, or a CJK id, has a different min-content width, and CJK in particular has break opportunities that Latin 'q' does not. The defect mechanism holds for any long unbreakable token, but the worst case is unmeasured and AC-1 fixes the fixture to keep the before/after contrast reproducible rather than maximal.

The narrow-viewport sweep runs headless with no forced-colors emulation. I judged a forced-colors browser check unnecessary — forced-colors forces colour and contrast, and does not alter overflow-wrap or intrinsic sizing, so a wrap that applies in the default mode applies there too — but that is reasoning, not a measurement, and the stylesheet does already carry a forced-colors carve-out for #main:focus.
validated_work_order.debate_summary:
The critique was right about the diagnosis and right about the one thing that mattered, and I upheld its blocking finding after reproducing it myself. Its strongest evidence is the read-site count: test/web/pages.test.js reads src/web/styles.css in eight places, the plan routed five, and the three it skipped include two pins — #main:focus and .page-title — that go green with their pinned declaration deleted outright and a comment left in its place. I ran the exact current regexes against both mutations and both read present. For a ticket whose entire subject is a class of false green, closing that class in five of eight sites while leaving three parsers behind is the same failure the ticket was filed for, one layer down. I upheld it and checked the marginal cost rather than taking it on faith: I prototyped the shared reader the plan had only asserted, ran it against the real stylesheet, and found 66 rules in source order, all nine pinned selectors resolving, nested at-rule rules emitted with their own selectors, zero spurious later overrides on the seven pins that gain a check, and the forced-colors ordering expressible from the new index data without the old `[^@]*?` regex. The cost is small and the alternative was indefensible, so this is the finding that changed the work order most.

I also upheld the two major findings, and they are the same class of error: both criteria would have been reported as passing on a tree where the fix was never applied. AC-3 said 'append the @media mutation, run the file, must be red' and claimed today's baseline is 72/72 green; the file is 71/72, red for an unrelated reason, so the criterion is satisfied by the baseline. AC-5 said the suite reads 471/471 while adding a test that makes it 472. Both are the plan stating a number it had not measured. I rewrote them to be discriminating — AC-3 by test name or failure count, AC-5 with the C-step intermediate (72/72, 471/471) stated separately from the final (73/73, 472/472).

The third major finding I upheld and adopted in the critic's preferred form rather than the plan's: the card pin's later-override loop is per-test local code, so migrating the parsers without lifting it would reintroduce the same blind spot on every pin the change touches and on the new .awaiting-list pin the ticket adds. I made it a third shared helper, `laterOverrides`, called by each pin with its own selector set, and verified that adding the check to the migrated pins passes green on the shipped stylesheet. Leaving it as a copy in each test would have been finding 6 reproduced inside the fix for finding 6 — eight parsers plus the copy the plan was adding right then.

From the minor findings I took the `i` flag on the ch-only regex (case-insensitive units are valid CSS and the flag costs nothing, so the narrowing should be about the unit and not the casing), and I took the seed-count correction: three pending, four seeded, one lapsed, not four pending. I did not take the `calc()` half of that finding — a calc() floor is not measurable by a test with no font, and failing loudly on a value the test cannot verify is the correct behaviour, so that is recorded in out_of_scope as an accepted cost rather than fixed.

What I dismissed, and why. From the missed-edge-case list: the forced-colors interaction with overflow-wrap. The argument is that Chromium honours author values under forced-colors and therefore a wrap might not apply — but forced-colors forces colour and contrast, not text layout or intrinsic sizing, so the inference does not carry to a layout property. I did not add a browser check for it; I recorded it in residual_risks as reasoning rather than measurement, because the stylesheet does carry a forced-colors carve-out and that is worth saying out loud. I also declined the suggestion that the new pin create its own decision rather than rely on the seed: the fragility is real but it is the same fragility the existing card pin already carries, both paths are constructible, and adding a fixture only this test uses is not an improvement over house convention. It is in residual_risks instead. From the regression-risk list, the notes about the stale docstring at pages.test.js:88-93 and the exact-selector-anchoring trap are both correct and both are now requirements in the files[] entry; the anchoring one is the highest-leverage line in the change, because an `includes()` lookup deletes rename protection across all eight pins at once and nothing else in the suite would notice.

One thing neither document had: the @keyframes step selectors. The stylesheet's `@keyframes skeleton-pulse` contributes `0%` and `100%` as rules in any brace-stack walk. They are harmless — every lookup is an exact selector match against a pinned selector — but I only found them because I ran the prototype, and a later reader who discovers them cold will reasonably assume they are a bug. They are now a comment requirement rather than a mystery.

Where I differ from both: I did not re-measure the browser figures. I have no browser driver, and I say in residual_risks that I took them from the proposal rather than reproducing them. What I did instead is confirm the defect from the CSS itself (.awaiting-list is display: grid, .awaiting-list li has no overflow-wrap) and note that two independent measurements at different fixture lengths agree on the mechanism. That is the main reason this is an 88 and not a 90 — along with the ch-only narrowing, which is a judgement about a test's strictness and not a verified defect, and which I upheld anyway because the reviewer's own text offered it and because accepting px is exactly how `min-width: 12px`, the original defect, stays green. A human who disagrees can overrule that one decision without touching the rest of this order.
